gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's own pairing rule for the MacBook Air: only 2022-or-later Airs fast-charge, they need a 70 W or higher USB PD source (67 W counts on the 13.6-inch only), the in-box USB-C to MagSafe 3 cable or a USB-C cable both qualify, and the 40 W (60 W max) adapter Apple ships with the current M5 Air is under that line. So a 100 W power-bank port charges the Air faster than its own charger, and a bank that drops to 65 W when shared does not fast-charge it.
standout_why: I compared against Macworld's review (cited), best-batteries' review (in the results, not cited) and the Notebookcheck launch piece for the Baseus. Macworld and best-batteries already give the UGREEN port split (100 W + 30 W with two devices; 115 W total with three) and Macworld's 56% in 30 minutes on an Air M3. Neither mentions Apple's 70 W threshold, which Air generations qualify, the 13.6-inch-only 67 W exception, MagSafe 3 or any cable pairing, or the wattage of the charger in the Air's box. The UGREEN US and Costco pages (both cited) returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so I could not compare against them directly.
decides: It confirms the UGREEN Nexode 20,000 mAh 130 W as the pick and separates it from our other 20K candidate. Macworld and best-batteries both report the UGREEN keeps 100 W on USB-C1 with a phone on USB-C2, which stays above Apple's 70 W line. Notebookcheck reports the Baseus EnerFill FC41 20K 100W gives one cable up to 65 W once several outputs are in use, which is under Apple's line for every Air (the 67 W exception is 13.6-inch only), so it wins only the built-in-cable, one-device-at-a-time segment. It also sets the page's exclusion cell: 2018–2021 Airs (Intel, M1) are not on Apple's fast-charge list, so a 100 W port buys them no speed. Our Baseus EnerFill FC11 20K 45 W could be offered to those owners outside the 100 W table, but I did not verify what those Airs actually draw.

findings.label: Which MacBook Airs fast-charge, and from what
findings.value: MacBook Air (2022 or later): 70 W, 96 W or 140 W USB-C power adapter with a USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable or USB-C charge cable; 67 W adapter on 13.6-inch models only; up to 50 percent battery in around 30 minutes
findings.source_title: Fast charge your MacBook Air or MacBook Pro - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's page is dated November 05, 2026. The list covers Apple adapters and displays; the only third-party entry is a display delivering 85 W. No Air before 2022 appears on it.

findings.label: Current MacBook Air (M5): fast-charge requirement, battery size, in-box charger and cable
findings.value: "Fast-charge capable with 70W or higher USB PD power source"; 13-inch 53.8 Wh, 15-inch 66.5 Wh; in the box: 40W Dynamic Power Adapter with 60W Max and USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable (2 m); MagSafe 3 port plus two Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports that support charging
findings.note: Arithmetic: the in-box adapter's 60 W maximum is under Apple's 70 W fast-charge line, and a 100 W bank port is over it. Apple words the requirement as any 'USB PD power source', so a PD power bank qualifies on wattage. A 72 Wh bank is 1.34× the 13-inch battery and 1.08× the 15-inch battery before conversion losses.

findings.label: Cable and adapter pairing by Air generation
findings.value: 2022 or later (MagSafe 3): 30 W (13-inch only), 35 W Dual, 67 W or 70 W adapter with USB-C to MagSafe 3 Cable, and these models can also charge with a USB-C charge cable; 2018 through 2021 (USB-C only): Apple 30W USB-C Power Adapter and USB-C Charge Cable. "You can charge your Mac with any USB-C power adapter or display, even if it provides higher or lower wattage"
findings.source_title: Identify your Mac power adapter / charge your Mac - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's page is dated May 21, 2026. It supports two cells: a 2022+ Air can use the bank's USB-C port with either the MagSafe 3 cable from its box or a USB-C cable; a 2018–2021 Air has USB-C only and Apple pairs it with a 30 W adapter.

findings.label: What each port gives alone and together (Macworld)
findings.value: USB-C1 100 W alone; USB-C2 30 W alone; USB-A 22.5 W; two devices 130 W maximum; with three devices USB-C2 and USB-A are throttled to a shared 15 W (115 W total); the allocation is fixed
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: Reviewer's figures, not UGREEN's page. The laptop port keeps 100 W with a phone attached, which is above Apple's 70 W line. Macworld gives the weight as 16.9 oz (480 g).

findings.label: Measured charge into a MacBook Air (Macworld)
findings.value: MacBook Air M3: 56% in 30 minutes on USB-C1
findings.source_title: Nexode Power Bank 20000mAh (130W) review: Compact, lightweight MacBook battery pack | Macworld
findings.note: This matches Apple's fast-charge rate of up to 50% in around 30 minutes. Macworld does not give the Air's screen size or say which cable was used (USB-C or MagSafe 3).

findings.label: PD version, recharge port and limits (best-batteries)
findings.value: USB-C1: up to 20 V 5 A (100 W), PD 3.0 with PPS 3.3–21 V; recharges only through USB-C1 at up to 65 W (20 V 3.25 A); delivered 54.8 Wh at 100 W to 64.7 Wh at 9 V 3 A against 72 Wh claimed; a 100 W load falls to 65 W or 45 W after 18 to 22 minutes
findings.source_title: Ugreen Nexode 20000 130W: Review, Real Wh and Limits - Best Batteries
findings.note: Best Batteries' measurements. Conflict to resolve on UGREEN's page: Macworld says the bank accepts up to 100 W input, though its reviewer saw no more than 70 W; Best Batteries says input is capped at 65 W. The in-box cable is described as about 50 cm with no wattage rating given.

findings.product: Baseus EnerFill FC41 Digital Display Power Bank 20000mAh 100W
findings.label: Built-in cable output alone and when shared (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: Two built-in USB-C cables, each up to 100 W alone; when multiple outputs are in use one USB-C cable gives up to 65 W and the remaining three outputs share 15 W; 65 W USB-C input, about 2 hours to full; 15.1 oz (about 428 g); 2.56 × 5.98 × 1.02 in
findings.source_title: Baseus releases new 20K power bank with display in US - Notebookcheck (Polly Allcock, 2025-11-13, updated 2026-02-17)
findings.note: A launch article restating Baseus's figures, not a test. 65 W is under Apple's 70 W line (and under the 67 W exception for the 13.6-inch), so the Air fast-charges from this bank only when nothing else is plugged in. Baseus's own estimate, as reported: MacBook Air 13 to 50% in half an hour and one full charge.
